speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have been experiencing fever and changes in your mental state for the last two days; can you tell me exactly what those mental changes look like and if you have had any seizures?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) secondary to haloperidol use, given the fever, altered mentation, history of tics, and absence of infectious symptoms like headache or sore throat. REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Head to rule out structural causes.
